However, E3 shows that nitriding can reduce fatigue strength in Ti-6Al-4V due to premature crack initiation, and the hypothesis cites only a higher-temperature (900 °C) failure while proposing 750 °C, which is closer to the problematic regime than the successful 600 °C case; the premise that 750 °C avoids such cracking is not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Plasma nitriding Ti-6Al-4V in NH3-N2 mixture at 750 °C forms a Ti-N compound layer ~2 μm thick
This layer increases surface hardness and eliminates stick-tear/plowing wear, reducing wear loss
The nitride layer and diffusion zone introduce compressive residual stresses that inhibit crack nucleation
Low-temperature nitriding (~600 °C) avoids premature crack initiation seen at higher temperatures
